sentences.sentence: Don’t I Know You?
As the fourth and final song faded, the DJ in our club at the north end of Waikiki kept the crowd pumped for another set of nude women on stage under the flashing black lights.
These men were mostly military dudes who were barely legal.
They were dancing around the perimeter of the stage, grooving to the music and laughing loudly.
I was standing next to my sister, her friend, and her friend’s brother, all of whom were similarly transfixed by the scene before us.
Suddenly, one of the dancers on stage turned and looked directly at me and said, “Don’t I know you?”
In that moment, my heart skipped a beat.
It seemed like fate had brought us together again, even if it was under such bizarre circumstances.
I stepped forward and replied, “Yes, you do.” And then she asked, “Where have I seen you?”
Her name is Sasha, and she works as a nurse in Boston.
She and I had met at a party back in college.
We both moved to New York City after graduation and lost touch over the years.
Now, here we were, 1000 miles apart, reunited by happenstance and coincidence in Hawaii.
It felt surreal, like a dream come true.
I quickly explained how we had met back in college, and she told me stories from her side of the story.
We laughed and reminisced about old times, and I was struck by how effortlessly we caught up.
It felt like no time had passed between our last meeting and this one.
She was just as charming and vivacious as she had been in college, and I was still the same laid-back and easy-going person I had always been.
After we finished our impromptu reunion, we spent the rest of the night catching up and dancing.
The atmosphere was electric, and the energy in the room was high.
The DJ kept the music going and the dancers moving until well past midnight.

sentences.sentence: Illustration by Fresh Idea
My Ego Sabotaged My Writing
Full manuscript in two months.
That was the goal.
I was on vacation in Mexico, no less, when I checked my email and saw the opportunity.
It was mid-June and the conference was happening near the end of September.

I had never attended one before, but I was eager to make the most of it and I envisioned myself walking up to the podium, confidently delivering my presentation and receiving enthusiastic applause from the audience.
As I settled into my beach chair under the Mexican sun, I began drafting a proposal for the conference.
My initial draft was three pages long—my usual length for these types of proposals.
After reviewing it, I realized that it was way too long.
I trimmed it down to two pages.
Still too long, I shortened it to one page.
Still not quite there, I edited it down to half a page.
At this point, I knew I needed to submit something substantial to stand a chance of being accepted, but I also didn’t want to give them a proposal that was too thin.
In the end, I submitted my proposal, which was exactly half a page long.
Fast forward two weeks, and I received an email from the conference organizers informing me that my proposal had been accepted.
Thrilled, I immediately started work on my presentation, but something felt off.
The more I wrote, the more I realized that my initial goal of having a full manuscript in two months was unrealistic.
I was writing at a snail's pace, my ideas weren’t flowing as smoothly as they once did, and my confidence was waning.
Every time I hit a roadblock, I told myself I could overcome it.
But the more roadblocks appeared, the more my ego took over and convinced me that I simply couldn’t do it.
I should have known better.
Ego can be a dangerous thing, especially when it comes to creative pursuits.

sentences.sentence: I woke up as a different person today.
I am an altogether different person this year.
But I still feel like the 13 year old me is watching me over.
I remember how she never wanted to grow up, thinking she would lose some of her essence, some of her innocence, some of her naivety, and perhaps some of her dreams, too.
Today, Sidra is turning 16, and I am reflecting on all that has happened since the last time I celebrated her birthday.
Sidra was always the epitome of innocence and purity.
She would come home from school wearing her favorite dress, humming tunes, and with a smile on her face.
She had a contagious energy and enthusiasm that made everyone around her feel alive and excited.
Her laughter was one of the most beautiful sounds in the world; it could lift spirits and bring joy to anyone who heard it.
She believed in magic, in love, and in the power of hope.
She was a dreamer, a visionary, and a fighter for what she believed in.
She would stand up for those who couldn’t stand up for themselves, and she would never let anyone bring her down or make her feel less than.
She was a force to be reckoned with, and yet she was also the sweetest person you could ever meet.
As she grew older, Sidra began to understand more about life and the world around her.
She started to see the not-so-perfect sides of people and situations, but she didn’t let it bring her down.
Instead, she used it as fuel to become even stronger and fight harder against injustice and inequality.
She became more independent, more confident, and more determined.
She started to see the world in a different way, but she still held onto her core values and principles.
She remained kind, compassionate, and optimistic, and she continued to dream big and aim high.

sentences.sentence: How prepared are you for the revolution?
Once upon a time, not that long ago in the restaurant, food, and hospitality industry, the formula for success was pretty simple to grasp.
Following the formula was widely accepted as the guaranteed path to making it big.
Sure, there were always some outliers that didn’t quite fit into the mold—those were typically seen as anomalies and not worthy of emulation.
But then came along a series of disruptions that have shaken up the very fabric of the hospitality industry and made everything we thought we knew about it turn on its head.

From the rise of online review platforms like Yelp and TripAdvisor, to the surge in popularity of mobile payments and contactless service, to the meteoric rise of ride-sharing services like Uber and Lyft, it seems like every aspect of the hospitality industry is being disrupted and redefined by new technology and consumer trends.
The hospitality industry has been hit hard by the global pandemic, which has forced many hotels, restaurants, and other businesses to shut down temporarily or permanently.
But even before the pandemic, the industry was already experiencing significant disruption.
One of the biggest disruptors has been the rise of online review platforms.
These platforms have given consumers a powerful tool to share their experiences and opinions about the places they visit.
This has put immense pressure on businesses to provide top-notch service and food quality to keep their online ratings high.
Another major disruptor has been the rise of mobile payments and contactless service.
With the rise of digital wallets like Apple Pay, Google Wallet, and Samsung Pay, consumers are increasingly using their smartphones to make purchases instead of carrying around cash or cards.
This has made it easier for customers to pay without having to wait in line or fumble through their purses to find their wallets.
It has also made it easier for businesses to process transactions quickly and efficiently.
One of the most significant recent disruptions in the hospitality industry has been the rise of ride-sharing services like Uber and Lyft.

sentences.sentence: The #1 Thing That Gets Me Through Difficult Days
My Coping Mechanism in Trying Times
Photo by Ian Chen on Unsplash
I remember the first few hours after my mother took her last breath.
I remember the first few days.
I remember the months and years that followed.
The days, weeks, and years have bled into one another, melding together like pieces of a puzzle that somehow just don’t fit.
Yet, amidst this mélange, there have been moments when the pieces seem to align and the picture forms—moments of clarity, moments of joy, moments of solace.
The first few hours after my mother’s passing was a blur.
I couldn’t comprehend what was happening.
I was in shock.
I remember staring blankly at the wall for hours on end.
I felt numb.
My mind wouldn’t process the reality of her passing.
It wasn’t real.
She was still here.
She would be back in just a minute.
She was going to call me from work.
She was going to be home soon.
She was still breathing.
It wasn’t until several days later that I began to realize the gravity of the situation.
I remember sitting in my car, parked outside her house, holding her photo and crying.
The realization hit me like a ton of bricks.
She was gone.
She was never coming back.
This was the moment when the weight truly began to settle in.
This was the moment when I understood the enormity of what had happened.
In those early days, the days were long and the nights were even longer.
I found myself in a constant state of mourning.
I didn’t know how to process it.
I didn’t know how to cope.
I didn’t know how to move forward.
Those early days were the most difficult days of my life.
But eventually, I began to find my way.
I began to find my footing.
I began to find my peace.

sentences.sentence: Vision 2020: The Well
Recordings, talk notes and application questions

Each week, we produce notes, discussion points and application questions for the Sunday talks — helping you go deeper into everything we’re looking at together and resourcing our discussions and reflections.
In a world that often emphasizes individualism and personal achievement, it’s easy to overlook the value of community and collective action.
However, in the context of Vision 2020, a global initiative aimed at preventing avoidable blindness and visual impairment, the importance of community and collective action becomes abundantly clear.

Vision 2020 is a global initiative launched in 1999 by the International Agency for the Prevention of Blindness (IAPB) with the goal of eliminating avoidable blindness and visual impairment by the year 2020.
Since its inception, significant progress has been made, but there is still much work to be done.
Vision 2020: The Well is a metaphor that encapsulates the idea of drawing upon the resources and strength of a community to achieve a common goal.
Just as a well provides a source of water for a community, Vision 2020 provides a source of support and resources for those who are working to eliminate avoidable blindness and visual impairment.
The well represents the collective effort and the shared resources that are necessary to achieve a common goal.
One of the key aspects of Vision 2020 is the emphasis on collaboration.
The initiative brings together organizations and individuals from all over the world to work towards the common goal of eliminating avoidable blindness and visual impairment.
This collaboration is essential because it allows for the sharing of resources and expertise, which can lead to more effective and efficient solutions.
For example, by working together, different organizations can share their knowledge and experience in preventing and treating different types of eye diseases.

sentences.sentence: Simple Changes That Helped Me Lose 5 Kg and Feel Great in Just One Month
Image by biscotto87
When the pandemic-induced lockdown happened, I lost all motivation.
My lifestyle became sedentary.
Up until then, I had been a regular gym-goer and followed a strict workout routine.
However, with everything closed down due to the lockdown, my routine went out of window, and I fell into a rut.
Despite trying to maintain some form of discipline, I found it difficult as there was nothing to look forward to.
This went on for several weeks, until one day, I decided enough was enough.
I realized that it wasn't just about physical fitness; it was also about mental health.
I needed to get back into a routine and start taking care of myself again.
So, I made some simple changes to my lifestyle, and within just one month, I managed to lose 5 kg and feel great.
Here’s how I did it:
1. **Set Realistic Goals**: The first step was to set realistic goals.
Instead of aiming for a major overhaul in my lifestyle, I decided to make small, manageable changes.
Setting realistic goals helped me stay motivated and not get demotivated easily.
2. **Dietary Changes**: The next change I made was to my diet.
I started tracking what I ate throughout the day.
I noticed that I was eating a lot of processed foods and sugary drinks.
This was not helping my health at all.
So, I decided to switch to healthier alternatives.
I started eating more vegetables, fruits, and lean proteins.
I also cut down on sugar and refined carbs.
These changes made a huge difference in how I felt.
3. **Hydration**: Another important aspect that I focused on was hydration.
I realized that I was not drinking enough water, which was leading to lethargy and low energy levels.
